title.en: Your first SIP, on the phone

text.en: {cast:banker} helps you finish [[kyc]] with your [[pan]] on the invest app. "Pick a fund. The Top-50 Index Fund is market-linked, so it goes up and down."

truth.en: No fixed return. Some years it falls 15–35%. It suits money you won't need for years.

label.en: Start a ₹500 monthly SIP in the Top-50 Index Fund

outcome.en: ₹500 a month. If it averages 10%, 15 years of this grows ₹90,000 into about ₹2 lakh.

why.en: An [[sip]] buys a few units every month, more when prices are low. Time does the heavy lifting.

label.en: Put ₹500 in the Short-term Debt Fund instead

outcome.en: About 6.5% a year with small swings. Steady, but slower for a goal 15 years away.

why.en: Debt funds suit goals 1–3 years away. Long goals usually need some growth.

label.en: Close the app. Shares are scary

hint.en: Every year you wait, the finish line moves.

outcome.en: ₹0 invested. The ₹500 a month goes to snacks and recharges instead.

why.en: A fund is not a single share. A small, steady SIP spreads the risk across 50 companies.

text.en: {cast:agent} has a new brochure. "Star Active Equity Fund! Last year it gave 28%! Much better than a boring index fund."

truth.en: Last year's star is often ordinary next year. Its 1.8% fee is charged every year, good or bad.
The Top-50 Index Fund charges 0.2% and pays Ramana no [[commission]]. That's why he calls it boring.

label.en: Put ₹5,000 in the Star Active Equity Fund through Ramana

outcome.en: At 10% before fees, ₹5,000 left for 20 years becomes about ₹24,200 after the 1.8% fee.

why.en: Fees come off every year. To be worth it, the manager must beat the index by more than the fee.

label.en: Compare fees, then buy the Top-50 Index Fund yourself

outcome.en: The same ₹5,000 for 20 years with a 0.2% fee: about ₹32,400. That's ₹8,200 more.

why.en: [[expense_ratio]] matters more than last year's return. Cheap and broad usually wins over time.

label.en: Ask Ramana for the fee and his commission first

outcome.en: "1.8%, and about 1% of it comes to me," he admits, reaching for the last vada. You keep your ₹5,000 for now.

why.en: Always ask how a seller is paid. It explains what they recommend.

text.en: A WhatsApp group adds you. "Spark Mobile will triple this month! Buy now at ₹60. 100% sure. Only for VIP members."

phrase.en: Spark Mobile will triple this month!

truth.en: Nobody knows next month's price. Groups like this buy first, hype it, then sell to you.
Registered advisers never promise returns. "Sure" tips are how pump-and-dump works.

label.en: Buy ₹10,000 of Spark Mobile now

hint.en: The group went quiet the day you bought.

outcome.en: You buy at ₹60. The group sells. It drops to ₹30, and you sell scared. ₹5,000 gone.

why.en: In a pump-and-dump, your buying is their exit. The tip was the product.

label.en: Leave the group and report it

outcome.en: ₹0 lost. Two weeks later Spark Mobile is back at ₹32. The group has a new name.

why.en: If someone sells "sure" tips, ask why they need your money to get rich.

label.en: Buy just ₹1,000 to test it

outcome.en: It halves, and the ₹20 brokerage stings too. ₹520 lost on a "small test".

why.en: A scam doesn't become safe in small amounts. It just teaches you more cheaply.

text.en: You have ₹20,000 saved. {cast:friend}: "My uncle's tractor is a Kisan. Put it all in Kisan Tractors shares, mama. Can't go wrong!"

truth.en: A good product isn't a safe share. One company can have a bad-news year and fall 30–60%.

label.en: Put all ₹20,000 in Kisan Tractors

outcome.en: If Kisan has a bad-news year, you lose ₹6,000 to ₹12,000. If not, it moves with the market.

why.en: A single share carries the company's own risks on top of the market's.

label.en: Put it in the Top-50 Index Fund

outcome.en: Kisan is about 2% of the fund. The same bad news would cost you about ₹200, not ₹10,000.

why.en: [[diversification]]: fifty companies rarely all have a bad year at once.

label.en: ₹2,000 in Kisan for fun, ₹18,000 in the index fund

outcome.en: Chintu is happy, and the worst Kisan news can now cost you about ₹1,200.

why.en: If you want a single share, keep it a small part of your money.

text.en: The bank's sales officer calls you in. "New fund launch! Only ₹10 a unit, very cheap. Old funds cost ₹80. Assured growth!"

truth.en: A low [[nav]] isn't cheaper. ₹1,000 grows the same 10% whether the unit costs ₹10 or ₹80.
Equity funds can't assure anything. A seller who says so is mis-selling.

label.en: Buy ₹10,000 of the new fund

outcome.en: 1,000 units at ₹10. Its fee is 1.8% a year, and it has no track record at all.

why.en: Judge a fund by its fee and what it holds, never by its unit price.

label.en: Ask for the fee, then pick the Top-50 Index Fund at ₹80 a unit

outcome.en: 125 units at ₹80, with a 0.2% fee. Same ₹10,000, 1.6% a year less in fees.

why.en: Fewer units at a higher NAV is fine. Growth is in percent, and fees decide what you keep.

label.en: Say no and leave

outcome.en: ₹0 spent. The officer's sales target is not your problem.

why.en: You can always walk away from a pitch.

title.en: The down payment, two years away

text.en: You have ₹50,000 for the dream's down payment, needed in two years. {cast:friend} says Spark Mobile could double it. {cast:banker} suggests a [[debt_fund]].

truth.en: It could also halve it, just when you need it. Shares suit goals many years away.

label.en: Short-term Debt Fund until the purchase

outcome.en: At about 6.6% a year, ₹50,000 is likely about ₹56,800 in two years, with small swings.

why.en: Match the product to the date. Money with a fixed date needs steady products.

label.en: All in Spark Mobile, to double it

hint.en: The seller of the plot won't wait for a recovery.

outcome.en: Spark is the most volatile share in town. A bad-news year could leave ₹20,000 to ₹35,000.

why.en: High risk with a short deadline means you may have to sell at the worst time.

label.en: Top-50 Index Fund

outcome.en: Could be ₹60,000, or ₹35,000 after a crash. In two years, nobody can say which.

why.en: Good for long goals, but two years is too short to ride out a crash.

text.en: The invest app is red. Your index fund is down from ₹60,000 to ₹48,000. The TV says "worst week in years, sell before it's too late".

truth.en: Nobody knows the bottom. Selling makes the fall permanent for you.

label.en: Hold, and keep the SIP running

outcome.en: You sleep badly for a month. Your ₹1,000 SIP now buys 25% more units than before.

why.en: For money you won't need for years, a fall is a sale. Panic is the expensive part.

label.en: Sell everything now

outcome.en: You lock in a ₹12,000 loss. The fall may reverse, but you won't be in it.

why.en: Selling in a crash turns a paper loss into a real one.

label.en: Move only the part needed next year to the debt fund

outcome.en: ₹15,000 for next year's need is now steady. ₹33,000 stays invested for the long run.

why.en: Near goals in safe products, far goals in growth. Decide by date, not by fear.
